facts.raw_span: episodes of spasms and tremors in her right hand and forearm
carpal tunnel release surgery initially
tremors recurred
progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability
No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case

T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles
T1-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI with contrast showed absence of contrast enhancement
Brain Biopsy (left frontal lesion): CD5− CD10− CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER−
Cytogenetic study: Normal female karyotype
Fluorescence in situ hybridization: Extra copies of BCL6 (3q27) and BCL2 (18q21), no MYC abnormalities
Cerebrospinal fluid: Presence of lymphoma cells
Bone marrow: Negative for lymphoma cells

rationales.F01: Initial presentation of spasms and tremors could be indicative of various neurological conditions.
rationales.F04: Progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability suggest a neurological condition with significant motor and coordination impairment.
rationales.F06: Extensive non-enhancing lesions in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres are highly suggestive of a lymphoma or other infiltrative process.
rationales.F08: Brain biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER- is diagnostic of a B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F10: Fluorescence in situ hybridization showing extra copies of BCL6 and BCL2 is consistent with a lymphoma.
rationales.F11: Presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid is diagnostic of central nervous system involvement by lymphoma.
rationales.F12: Absence of lymphoma cells in the bone marrow suggests that the lymphoma is primarily confined to the central nervous system.
